content:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach on /v1/generate (canary pool). Current p99=1.9s (SLO 1.0s). Paging oncall group: @oncall-runtime :rotating_light:

sam (oncall): I’m on it. seeing spike on canary pool only?

mike-sre: confirming — canary-gpu-pool-7 shows increased tail latency and lots of streaming stalls. node-level GPU mem pressure up ~30% vs baseline.

jess-eng: rolling v5->v5b started ~10m ago, 10% traffic to canary. Correlates with the spike.

noah-ml: v5b changed attention cache layout (KV layout v2). Might increase KV cache misses for short-context streaming. Could explain stalls.

sam (oncall): tagging @noah-ml and @jess-eng. Quick mitigation: reduce canary traffic to 1-2% and enable automatic fallback to v4.

jess-eng: doing `redwood routing set --service inference-api --env canary --percent 2` now (cli).

leah-prodops: also toggling model fallback: `redwood models set-fallback --service inference-api --fallback-version v4`

incident-bot: ROUTING_CHANGE: canary traffic set to 2% by sam at 1971234630

anna-support: Customers reporting increased latency for a handful of sessions (some streaming stalls), estimated impacted requests ~0.6% of prod traffic. Opening a customer impact note.

sam (oncall): can we confirm KV cache miss rate on canary vs baseline?

mike-sre: pulling metrics, quick query: 
```
sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total{pool=~"canary.*"}[1m])) by (pool)
```
results: canary pool miss rate ~4.7x baseline. Also seeing higher tail queue_length for streamer threads.

noah-ml: that's consistent with the KV layout change. If misses cause more backend fetches it raises latency for streaming token emits.

jess-eng: options: a) rollback canary to v4, b) keep canary but reduce concurrency and increase replica count, c) patch runtime to accept both kv layouts (hotfix). Fastest is rollback.

sam (oncall): prefer rollback for customer-facing SLO. I'll coordinate. Who can execute rollback?

jess-eng: I can. Command: `redwood deploy rollback --service inference-api --from v5b --to v4 --force` (starts now).

incident-bot: DEPLOY_ROLLBACK initiated by jess-eng at 1971234755

mike-sre: during rollback we should also drain canary nodes to avoid mixing caches: `kubectl label node canary-7 evict=true` then `kubectl cordon node/canary-7` — doing that now.

anna-support: posting brief to customers: "We detected a canary model change causing a temporary increase in latency for a small subset of requests. We’ve reduced canary traffic and rolled back the canary; monitoring continues."

sam (oncall): rollback finished — routing shows canary traffic 0% and active model versions back to v4 cluster-wide. See `redwood routing status --service inference-api` output: 
```
canary: 0% -> v5b (inactive)
prod: 100% -> v4
```
incident-bot: ROLLBACK_COMPLETE at 1971234890

mike-sre: post-rollback metrics: p99 dropped to 0.85s within 2 minutes, KV miss rate returned to baseline, streaming stall count dropped by 92%.

noah-ml: thanks team. I'll push a small instrumented build of v5b that keeps the old KV layout flag-enabled to test without changing runtime.

jess-eng: logging follow-up items: 1) add rollout preflight test for KV cache behavior, 2) add automated pre-rollout traffic limiter that starts at 0.5% for 5m, 3) add canary throttle runbook.

sam (oncall): noted. Assigning follow-ups to eng and ml. @leah-prodops can you own the canary throttle runbook doc?

leah-prodops: yup I'll draft and link to runbook. Also recommend adding a short-term alert: canary_p99 > prod_p99 * 1.5 -> auto-throttle.

anna-support: customers updated. No escalations so far. Logging incident in tracker INC-1971 and will add incident impact summary.

sam (oncall): handing off to oncall-next at 1971235467 — summary: canary-induced p99 surge, reduced traffic, rolled back, metrics recovered. If anything flares, page the runtime oncall. Good job. :thumbsup:

jess-eng: nice coordination. I'll open a PR for the preflight tests and tag @noah-ml.

noah-ml: will add regression evals for streaming microbenchmarks.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (monitoring) at 1971235467
